claim_as_stated: PF grants to sponsors are flows into the DAF system from outside, not double counts with DAF-to-DAF
exact_values_found: The DAF-to-DAF file reads Form 990 Schedule I only; the PF file reads 990-PF Part XV only, so no row can be in both. Two panel sponsors filed 990-PFs: Jasper Ridge Charitable Fund (final §507(b)(1)(A) TY2023: $2,956,978 to Schwab and $1,249,438 to Fidelity, T1) and Every.org (TY2024: $505,226 to Network for Good and Edward Charles Foundation, T2).
discrepancies: In substance the Jasper Ridge and Every.org lines are sponsor-to-sponsor transfers ($4.7m, 0.03% of T1-T3), not PF money.
interpretation_challenge: A PF grant to a sponsor is a contribution to the sponsor and later a DAF grant; the study correctly does not net it.

claim_as_stated: Recipient fund names are cut at the first separator so FBO person tails are dropped; no individual is profiled
exact_values_found: Recipient_name_filed and purpose_text still carry names of individual DAF holders and donors where the name leads the string, e.g. a Fidelity giving account of a named couple, a Schwab fund listed with two named donors, named family DAFs and in-memory purposes. A tight heuristic (first name, initial, surname next to DAF/FUND words) flags 176 return-sponsor rows (22 in recipient_name_filed, 154 in purpose_text); most hand-read examples are real personal names.
discrepancies: The §4 privacy statement is not accurate for the CSV as published.
interpretation_challenge: Foundation names (pf_name) are organisations and acceptable. Recommend blanking purpose_text or replacing named-fund text with a DAF flag, and cutting recipient_name_filed to the matched brand. The scratch summary JSON's unmatched_review also carries a person name in an ATTN tail (not in the repo).
